nodes.title: SG-1.1 Define the shared palette and 480x270 render constants
nodes.body:
Context: game/frontend/src/phaser/config.ts exports GAME_WIDTH=640 and GAME_HEIGHT=360 and computeZoom. No palette module exists. tailwind.config.ts only maps HSL CSS variables. Desired behavior: a single palette file lists at most 48 hex colours in named warm and cool ramps, exported as constants and as Tailwind colours; config.ts uses 480x270; computeZoom is unit tested for whole-number zoom across window sizes and DPR values. Expected result: later SG-1.2 and SG-1.3 art code and UI tokens can import one palette and one render size. Why: the pixel-art overhaul needs a single source of truth for colour and native resolution.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the palette module, when its colours are counted, then there are at most 48 unique hex values grouped in named warm and cool ramps.
- Given the palette module, when imported by Tailwind config, then each palette colour is available as a Tailwind colour.
- Given config.ts, when read, then GAME_WIDTH is 480 and GAME_HEIGHT is 270 and buildGameConfig uses them.
- Given several window sizes and DPR values, when computeZoom runs, then it returns a whole number of at least 1.
- Given the existing test suite, when run for the touched files, then no test assumes 640x360.


## Scope
- In scope: Palette module
- In scope: Tailwind colour export
- In scope: 480x270 constants
- In scope: computeZoom tests
- Out of scope: Grid-to-pixel functions (SG-1.2)
- Out of scope: PNG script and manifest update (SG-1.3)
- Out of scope: New rooms, story content, backend, audio, deployment, repo clean-up
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin and its guard tests
- Preserve: Existing hsl Tailwind tokens
- Preserve: pixelArt, roundPixels and FIT scale settings


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix, Zustand stay.
- One native scene resolution of 480x270, whole-number scaling, nearest-neighbour.
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once.
- Tests are unit tests with dependencies mocked.


## Definition of done
- All requirements below delivered with passing unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · One palette file defines at most 48 colours in warm and cool ramps and exports constants
nodes.body:
Context: no palette exists in game/frontend/src. Desired behavior: game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts defines 8 ramps of 6 hex colours (4 warm: wood, brass, parchment, lamp; 4 cool: indigo, plum, moon, hoodie), exported as PALETTE_RAMPS, a flat PALETTE array and WARM_RAMPS / COOL_RAMPS name lists. Expected result: any module imports the same colours. Why: art and UI must share one palette.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given PALETTE, when its length is read, then it is at most 48 and every entry matches /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/.
- Given PALETTE, when deduplicated, then no colour repeats.
- Given WARM_RAMPS and COOL_RAMPS, when read, then each name exists in PALETTE_RAMPS and the two lists do not overlap.


## Scope
- In scope: palette.ts constants
- Out of scope: Using the palette in art code
- Preserve: Existing CSS variables


## Technical constraints
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once and used by art and UI.


## Definition of done
- palette.ts exists and exports the constants


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · The palette is exported as Tailwind colours
nodes.body:
Context: tailwind.config.ts L4 extends colors with hsl(var(--x)) tokens only. Desired behavior: palette.ts exports paletteTailwindColors (ramp name -> step 1..6 -> hex) and tailwind.config.ts adds it under colors.pal, giving classes such as bg-pal-wood-3. Expected result: UI can use palette colours via utilities. Why: UI and art must use the same colours.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given paletteTailwindColors, when read, then every PALETTE colour appears exactly once as a value.
- Given tailwind.config, when theme.extend.colors.pal is read, then it equals paletteTailwindColors.
- Given tailwind.config, when theme.extend.colors.background is read, then it is still hsl(var(--background)).


## Scope
- In scope: paletteTailwindColors export
- In scope: tailwind.config.ts colors.pal
- Out of scope: Replacing existing tokens
- Out of scope: Restyling components
- Preserve: Existing token colours and content globs
- Preserve: tailwindConfig.test.ts expectations


## Technical constraints
- Tailwind stays; palette defined once and reused, not duplicated.


## Dependencies
- REQ-PAL


## Definition of done
- Tailwind config exposes pal colours


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Render constants are 480x270 and computeZoom always returns a whole number of at least 1
nodes.body:
Context: config.ts has 640x360 and computeZoom returns NaN when dpr is NaN (Math.max(1, NaN)). Desired behavior: GAME_WIDTH=480, GAME_HEIGHT=270, computeZoom treats non-finite or non-positive dpr as 1 and floors to an integer of at least 1. Expected result: whole-number zoom for any window size and DPR. Why: pixel-perfect rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given config.ts, when GAME_WIDTH and GAME_HEIGHT are read, then they are 480 and 270 and buildGameConfig width/height equal them.
- Given (1280,720,1), (1920,1080,1), (1920,1080,2), (1366,768,1), (1280,720,1.5), when computeZoom runs, then results are 2, 4, 8, 2, 4.
- Given (479,269,1) or dpr 0, NaN or negative, when computeZoom runs, then the result is 1.


## Scope
- In scope: config.ts constants
- In scope: computeZoom dpr guard
- Out of scope: Changing scale mode
- Out of scope: PhaserHost behaviour
- Preserve: pixelArt, roundPixels, antialias false, FIT, zoom parameter
- Preserve: PhaserHost use of computeZoom


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x.
- One native scene resolution of 480x270, whole-number scaling, nearest-neighbour.


## Definition of done
- Constants changed and computeZoom guarded


## Clarifying questions
- None

const ratio = Number.isFinite(dpr) && dpr > 0 ? dpr : 1;
return Math.max(1, Math.floor(Math.min((w * ratio) / GAME_WIDTH, (h * ratio) / GAME_HEIGHT)));
